subject: Approvals + resourcing: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated capacity)
related_links: Confluence: ADR-0143 Config validation policy gates
body:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 13, 2026 at 8:42 AM
Subject: Approvals + resourcing: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated capacity)

Vanessa + Lauren,

I want to lock approvals + resourcing today so we can start the Provision-to-ready automation sprint next Monday without thrash.

Goal (what we’re committing to): reduce Dedicated “time-to-ready” by automating the full bring-up lifecycle (provision → image → bootstrap → validate → Ready) with stage metrics and explicit readiness gates.

Timeline proposal (single sprint with pilot):
- Week 1: baseline + failure-mode inventory; agree on readiness definition + stage budgets; finalize ADRs
- Week 2: orchestration primitives (IaC wrapper, image build hooks, config validation) + initial metrics
- Week 3: readiness gates + perf-canary integration + control-plane Ready transition; dashboards/alerts
- Week 4: pilot on 1–2 internal pools + 1 customer expansion; runbooks; retro

Explicit ownership asks (need yes/no today):
1) Sprint engineering lead / day-to-day: Vanessa
2) Product owner / messaging for Sales/CS on what “Ready” means + timeline expectations: Lauren
3) Exec sponsor / tie-breaker + staffing authority: me

Resourcing request (minimum viable):
- Infra/Fleet: 2 eng full-time for weeks 2–4 (Gabe + Victor on pipeline + networking checks; Nina consulting on topology)
- SRE: 1 eng half-time weeks 2–4 (time-to-ready metrics + alerting policy; also readiness gate failure taxonomy)
- Platform/Control Plane/Routing: 1 eng full-time weeks 2–3, half-time week 4 (Ready state semantics + API + routing gating)

Notes / constraints:
- We need a break-glass mechanism for config validation (audited). Security sign-off required before we flip the feature flag in prod.
- Multi-region + mixed GPU SKUs are a must; no SKU-specific assumptions.
- Safe rollout: stage-by-stage manual override, clear rollback points.

Questions for you both:
- Can you confirm the resourcing above is realistic? If not, what’s the smallest set that still produces a meaningful pilot?
- Lauren: are there specific Dedicated commitments (customer-facing) that this sprint must not jeopardize?

If you’re aligned, I’ll ask Neha to bless the staffing trade-offs and we’ll publish the on-point schedule.

—
Irene Choi
Director, Infrastructure Engineering
Redwood Inference



From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 13, 2026 at 9:11 AM
Subject: Re: Approvals + resourcing: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated capacity)

I’m in to lead.

On resourcing: Infra side is workable if we can pull Gabe full-time for W2–W4 (he’s currently split with another queue). Victor can be 50–75% as long as we keep networking checks focused (DNS/TLS + egress + basic reachability).

Big risk if we don’t have a dedicated Platform owner for Ready semantics + routing gate. We can build the pipeline and still be stuck arguing about “Validating vs Ready” or which system is source of truth.

Suggestion: lock a single “state machine owner” even if implementation spans repos.

Also: I’d like to bake in the “escape hatch” from day 1 (break-glass + audit log), otherwise we’ll slow down pilots when schema validation hits edge cases.

Vanessa
Engineering Manager, Fleet Automation



From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 13, 2026 at 9:37 AM
Subject: Re: Approvals + resourcing: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated capacity)

Aligned on the goal and timeline.

Customer commitments / constraints:
- We have two Dedicated expansion asks in flight where Sales has already used “~2 weeks” informally. If we can get to a reliable, measurable “< 72 hours in 80% of cases” for expansions, that’s a huge win—but I don’t want us promising anything externally until we have a pilot datapoint.
- Messaging needs to be crisp: “Ready” means routable capacity with perf sanity checks complete; “Provisioned” is not a customer milestone.

I can own the messaging + internal enablement (Sales/CS ETA language, what we show in Console vs what stays internal).

One request: please make sure the pilot includes one real customer expansion (with comms + rollback plan), not only internal pools, or we’ll get into an endless “it worked in staging” loop.

Lauren
Director of Product, Dedicated



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 13, 2026 at 10:04 AM
Subject: Re: Approvals + resourcing: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated capacity)

I’m supportive, with one condition: I want explicit named owners per stage and a weekly checkpoint with a measurable delta (even if it’s “baseline only” in week 1).

Please send:
1) The stage breakdown you’re using (Requested → Provisioning → Imaging → Bootstrapping → Validating → Ready/Failed)
2) Stage budgets (what “good” looks like, p50/p95 targets)
3) A list of what gets de-prioritized to free the headcount

On staffing trade-offs: I’m OK moving people for 4 weeks if we’re not creating a long-term operational burden.

-Neha



From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 13, 2026 at 10:32 AM
Subject: Re: Approvals + resourcing: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated capacity)

Agreed.

1) Stage breakdown (proposed state machine):
- Requested
- Provisioning (Terraform/IaC + cloud resources)
- Imaging (golden image apply + driver/runtime prereqs)
- Bootstrapping (k8s/bootstrap components + registration)
- Validating (smoke tests + networking checks + GPU health + perf-canary)
- Ready (routable) / Failed (operator intervention required)

2) Stage budgets (initial targets; we’ll baseline in W1):
- Provisioning: <= 60m p50 / <= 120m p95
- Imaging: <= 45m p50 / <= 90m p95
- Bootstrapping: <= 30m p50 / <= 60m p95
- Validating: <= 30m p50 / <= 45m p95
- Total time-to-ready (expansion): <= 3h p50 / <= 6h p95

Caveat: new pool creation might remain longer depending on quotas/region—our primary win is expansions and “known path” pools.

3) What we’re de-prioritizing to free headcount:
- Two non-urgent fleet UX improvements (internal CLI cleanups not required for pilot)
- A small backlog of Dedicated pool “manual checklist” polish (to be replaced by automation)

Vanessa and I will publish named owners per stage in Linear (ENG-2741) and in the Confluence overview.

Open item: we still need to lock a Platform owner for Ready state semantics + routing gating. I’m working that separately today.

Irene



From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 13, 2026 at 11:18 AM
Subject: Re: Approvals + resourcing: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated capacity)

Adding proposed stage owners (draft):
- Provisioning (IaC wrapper + idempotency): Gabe Wilson
- Imaging (golden image hooks + promote/rollback): Sahana Iyer (consult) + Gabe as implementer
- Bootstrapping (helm chart pinning + bootstrap hooks): Nina Petrova (architecture review) + Gabe
- Validating:
  - networking checks: Victor Alvarez
  - GPU health + smoke tests: Gabe
  - perf-canary integration: Rina Kobayashi (consult/PR review)
- Metrics/dashboards: Logan Wright (consult) + Aisha Bello (SRE owner)

Operator docs/runbooks: Kira Thompson (needs 20–30% time starting week 3)

If Platform owner is not available full-time, we can still implement “Ready” write path behind a feature flag but routing gate will slip. That’s the biggest dependency.

Vanessa



From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 4:56 PM
Subject: Re: Approvals + resourcing: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated capacity)

Update: I can’t yet confirm a Platform engineer allocation for weeks 2–3.

Given that, I want to propose a contingency plan so we don’t burn the sprint:
- We proceed with the provisioning pipeline + state machine + readiness gates and produce a “Ready candidate” state.
- Routing gate changes are week 3–4 stretch, pending staffing.
- For pilot: we keep new pools out of routing manually (explicit “do not advertise” toggle) until the routing integration is done.

Lauren: does this still meet your bar for a customer pilot if we’re explicit that routability is still manually controlled?

Neha: if Platform staffing remains blocked, I may come back asking for an explicit exec-level decision to trade off one Platform roadmap item.

Irene



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 16, 2026 at 5:28 PM
Subject: Re: Approvals + resourcing: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated capacity)

Proceed with the contingency plan, but make the dependencies visible.

Requirements for week 1 close:
- A single-page “RACI” for each stage + the Ready definition (who sets it, who consumes it, who can override)
- A short list of “manual controls” we’re relying on during the pilot (and how they’ll be audited)

Lauren: please make sure Sales/CS messaging does not imply routability until routing gating is actually shipped.

Irene: if Platform staffing is still blocked after week 1, bring me the trade-off options and I’ll force the decision.

-Neha
